Āsavagocchaka (The Group on the Taints)
Section on Analysis:
Root Condition.
Dependent upon a state that is an outflow, an outflowing state arises by way of the root condition: dependent upon the outflow of sensual desire, the outflow of views [arises].

The taint of ignorance; dependent on the taint of views, there is the taint of sensual desire and the taint of ignorance; dependent on the taint of ignorance, there is the taint of sensual desire and the taint of views;
dependent on the taint of existence, there is the taint of ignorance; dependent on the taint of views, there is the taint of ignorance. (Each wheel should be constructed in this manner.
Dependent on a state that is a taint, a state that is not a taint arises by way of root condition: dependent on a taint, the aggregates associated with the taint and mind-produced matter arise.

Dependent on a state that is an *āsava*, states that are both *āsava* and not-*āsava* arise by way of root condition: dependent on the *āsava* of sensual desire (*kāmāsava*), there arise the *āsava* of views (*diṭṭhāsava*), the *āsava* of ignorance (*avijjāsava*), the associated aggregates, and mind-produced matter.
(The cycle continues. Dependent on a state that is not an *āsava*, a state that is not an *āsava* arises by way of root condition:
dependent on one aggregate that is not an *āsava*, there arise three aggregates and mind-produced matter … [and so on] … dependent on two aggregates … [and so on] … at the moment of rebirth-linking.
...pe... dependent on the aggregates, there is the [heart-]base; dependent on the [heart-]base, there are the aggregates; one great primary element ...pe...
dependent on the great primary elements, there is mind-produced matter, kamma-born matter, and derived matter.
Dependent on a state that is not an outflow (anāsava), a state that is an outflow (āsava) arises by way of the root condition: dependent on the aggregates that are not outflows, the outflows arise.

Dependent on a state that is not an *āsava*, states that are both *āsava* and not *āsava* arise by way of root condition: dependent on one aggregate that is not an *āsava*, three aggregates, the *āsavas*, and mind-produced matter arise … [and so on] … dependent on two aggregates … [and so on] ….

Dependent on a state that is both an *āsava* and not an *āsava*, an *āsava* state arises by way of root condition: dependent on the *kāmāsava* and its associated aggregates, the *diṭṭhāsava* and *avijjāsava* arise. (The wheel should be constructed.)

Dependent on a state that is both an *āsava* and not an *āsava*, a state that is not an *āsava* arises by way of root-condition (*hetupaccaya*): dependent on one aggregate that is not an *āsava* and the *āsavas*, the [other] three aggregates and mind-originated matter arise … [and so on for] two aggregates … Dependent on a state that is both an *āsava* and not an *āsava*, states that are both *āsava* and not an *āsava* arise by way of root-condition:
dependent on one aggregate that is not an *āsava* and the *kāmasava*, the [other] three aggregates, the *diṭṭhāsava*, the *avijjāsava*, and mind-originated matter arise.
Form …pe… two aggregates …pe….
Chapter on Enumeration:
Pure.

In the case of cause-condition: nine; in the case of object-condition: nine (nine in all cases); in the case of resultant-condition: one; in the case of nutriment-condition: nine ... pe ... in the case of non-disappearance-condition: nine. Positive (Anuloma). 2.3.1.1.2. Negative (Paccanīya) of Conditions.
Section on Analysis:

Dependent on a state that is not a cause and is not an outflow, there arises a state that is not a cause and is not an outflow, by way of the root-cause condition— that is, a rootless state that is not an outflow.

Dependent on one aggregate, there arise three aggregates and mind-produced matter … two aggregates … [and so on] … At the moment of rootless rebirth-linking … dependent on the aggregates, there arises the [heart-]base; dependent on the [heart-]base, there arise the aggregates;
one great primary … [and so on] … up to non-percipient beings.

Dependent on a state that is not an *āsava*, a state that is an *āsava* arises by way of the not-root condition (*nahetupaccaya*): dependent on the aggregates associated with doubt and associated with restlessness, there arises delusion associated with doubt and associated with restlessness.
Dependent on a state that is an *āsava*, a state that is not an *āsava* arises by way of the not-object condition (*naārammaṇapaccaya*): dependent on the *āsavas*, mind-originated matter arises.
Dependent on a state that is not an outflow, a state that is not an outflow arises by way of object condition:
dependent on aggregates that are not outflows, mind-produced matter [arises]; at the moment of rebirth-linking …pe… dependent on the aggregates, the [heart-]base;
one great primary …pe… (up to non-percipient beings).

Dependent on a state that is both an *āsava* and not an *āsava*, a state that is not an *āsava* arises by way of object condition: dependent on *āsava*s and their associated aggregates, mind-produced matter arises. (Abbreviated.
Numerical Section:
Pure.
With not-root, two; with not-object, three; with not-predominance, nine; with not-proximity, three; with not-contiguity, three;
with not-mutuality, three; with not-strong-dependence, three; with not-prenascence, nine; with not-postnascence, nine; with not-repetition, nine;
with not-kamma, three; with not-resultant, nine; with not-nutriment, one; with not-faculty, one; with not-jhāna, one; with not-path, [one].
One [condition], three for non-association, nine for non-dissociation, three for non-absence, and three for non-disappearance. The Negative (Paccanīya). 2.3.1.1.3.
Positive-Negative (Paccayānulomapaccanīya).
Hetuduka: With root condition, there are three [answers] for non-object; nine for non-predominance; three for non-proximity; three for non-contiguity;
three for non-mutuality; three for non-strong-dependence; nine for non-prenascence; nine for non-postnascence; [nine] for non-repetition.

With the root condition, there are nine; with the kamma condition, three; with the resultant condition, nine; with the association condition, three; with the dissociation condition, nine; with the absence condition, three;
with the disappearance condition, three.
This is the positive-negative method (anuloma-paccanīya).
2.3.1.1.4. Positive Order of the Negative Condition (Paccayapaccanīyānuloma) Non-root Dyad (Nahetuduka):
With non-root condition, there are two [types] for object, two for proximity …pe… one for resultant …pe… one for path …pe… two for non-disappearance.
Negative-Positive (Paccanīyānuloma).
2.3.1.2. The Chapter on Conascent (Sahajātavāra):
The Chapter on Conascent is the same as the Chapter on Dependent (Paṭiccasamuppādavāra).
2.3.1.3. Section on Conditions (Paccayavāra) 2.3.1.3.1.
Positive Exposition of Conditions (Paccayānuloma Vibhaṅgavāra)
Conditioned by a state that is a *āsava*, a state that is an *āsava* arises by way of root-condition. (Three based on *āsava*;

similar to the *paṭicca* [dependent origination] formula. Conditioned by a state that is not an *āsava*, a state that is not an *āsava* arises by way of root-condition: conditioned by one aggregate that is not an *āsava*...

Conditioned by [one] aggregate, there arise three aggregates and mind-produced matter …pe… conditioned by two aggregates …pe… at the moment of rebirth-linking …pe… conditioned by the aggregates, there arises the [heart-]base;

conditioned by the [heart-]base, there arise the aggregates; conditioned by the great primaries, there arise mind-produced matter, kamma-produced matter, and derived matter; conditioned by the [heart-]base, there arise the outflow-free aggregates.

Conditioned by a state that is not an *āsava*, an *āsava* state arises by way of root condition: conditioned by *anāsava* aggregates, the *āsavas* arise; conditioned by the [heart-]base, the *āsavas* arise.
Conditioned by a state that is not an *āsava*, both *āsava* and *anāsava* states arise by way of root condition:
conditioned by one *anāsava* aggregate, three aggregates, the *āsavas*, and mind-produced matter arise … [and so on] … conditioned by two aggregates … [and so on].
...pe... conditioned by the [corrupt] basis (*vatthu*), the taints (*āsava*) and the associated aggregates arise.
Conditioned by a state that is both a taint and not a taint, a taint state arises by way of root-condition (*hetupaccaya*):

conditioned by the taint of sensual desire (*kāmāsava*) and the associated aggregates, the taint of views (*diṭṭhāsava*) and the taint of ignorance (*avijjāsava*) [arise] (the cycle). Conditioned by the taint of sensual desire and the [corrupt] basis...
Conditioned by the taint of views and the taint of ignorance, [the remaining taints arise]. (The Wheel.
Conditioned by a state that is both a taint and not a taint, a state that is not a taint arises by way of root condition:
conditioned by one aggregate that is not a taint and the taints, three aggregates and mind-produced matter arise …pe… conditioned by two aggregates [and the taints] …pe….
... [as before] ... conditioned by an *āsava* (taint) and its basis, there arise aggregates that are not *āsavas*.
Conditioned by a phenomenon that is both an *āsava* and not an *āsava*, phenomena that are both an *āsava* and not an *āsava* arise by way of the root-condition (*hetupaccaya*):

conditioned by one aggregate that is not an *āsava* and the *kāmāsava* (sensual-taint), there arise three aggregates, the *diṭṭhāsava* (view-taint), the *avijjāsava* (ignorance-taint), and mind-originated [matter].
Form …pe… two aggregates …pe… (the cycle). Conditioned by the taint of sensual desire and the physical basis, there arise the taint of views, the taint of ignorance, and the associated aggregates.
Chapter on Enumeration.

In the pure (suddha) relation of cause, there are nine; in the object (ārammaṇa), nine; in the predominance (adhipati), nine ... pe ... in the resultant (vipāka), one ... pe ... in non-disappearance (avigata), nine.
Positive (anuloma).

2.3.1.3.2. Analysis of the Section on Negative Conditions (Paccayapaccanīya Vibhaṅgavāra) Conditioned by a state that is not an outflow (noāsava), a state that is not an outflow arises by way of the root-cause condition (nahetupaccaya): [namely,] a rootless state that is not an outflow.

Conditioned by one aggregate, there arise three aggregates and mind-produced matter … two aggregates … pe … at the moment of rootless rebirth-linking … pe … (up to the non-percipient beings) conditioned by the eye-base,
eye-consciousness arises … pe … conditioned by the body-base, body-consciousness arises … conditioned by the [heart-]base, rootless aggregates that are not outflows arise.

Conditioned by a state that is not an *āsava*, an *āsava* state arises by way of the not-root condition (*nahetupaccaya*): conditioned by the aggregates accompanied by doubt and accompanied by restlessness, and the [heart-]base, doubt-accompanied and restlessness-accompanied delusion (*moha*) arises.

2.3.1.5. Chapter on Conjoined (Saṁsaṭṭhavāra) 2.3.1.5.1–4. Positive Conditionality, etc. (Paccayānulomādi):

A state that is an *āsava* (taint), being conjoined with [another] state that is an *āsava*, arises by way of the root condition (*hetupaccaya*). For example: the taint of sensual desire (*kāmāsava*) being conjoined with the taint of views (*diṭṭhāsava*) and the taint of ignorance (*avijjāsava*).
In the case of root-cause, nine; in the case of object, nine (nine in all cases); in the case of resultant, one …pe… in the case of non-disappearance, nine.

In the case of not-root, two; in the case of not-predominance, nine; in the case of not-prenascence, nine; in the case of not-postnascence, nine; in the case of not-repetition, nine; in the case of not-kamma, three; in the case of not-resultant, nine; in the case of not-jhāna, one; in the case of not-path, one;
in the case of not-dissociation, nine. 2.3.1.6. The Section on Association (Sampayutta-vāra)

Section on Analysis:

Root Condition. A state that is an *āsava* is a condition for a state that is an *āsava* by way of the root condition—namely, the *āsava* of sensual desire is a condition for the *āsava* of views and the *āsava* of ignorance by way of the root condition; the *āsava* of existence is a condition for the *āsava* of ignorance by way of the root condition. (The Wheel.)

A state that is an *āsava* is a condition for a state that is not an *āsava* by way of the root-condition (*hetu-paccaya*): the roots that are *āsavas* are a condition by way of the root-condition for their associated aggregates and for mind-produced matter.
A state that is an *āsava* is a condition for both a state that is an *āsava* and a state that is not an *āsava* by way of the root-condition:

the *āsava* of sensual desire (*kāmāsava*) is a condition by way of the root-condition for the *āsava* of views (*diṭṭhāsava*), the *āsava* of ignorance (*avijjāsava*), their associated aggregates, and mind-produced matter.
Conditioned by way of root-condition (*hetu-paccaya*).

A state that is not an outflow (*anāsava*) is related to a state that is not an outflow by way of root-condition: roots that are not outflows are related to their associated aggregates and to mind-produced matter by way of root-condition; at the moment of rebirth-linking... [etc.
...A state that is not an outflow is related to a state that is an outflow by way of root-condition: roots that are not outflows are related to their associated outflows by way of root-condition.

A state that is not an outflow (anāsava) is a condition, by way of root-condition (hetu-paccaya), for a state that is both an outflow and not an outflow: roots that are not outflows are a condition, by way of root-condition, for associated aggregates, for the outflows, and for mind-produced matter. States that are both an outflow and not an outflow are conditions, by way of root-condition, for a state that is not an outflow: roots that are both outflows and not outflows are a condition, by way of root-condition, for associated aggregates, for the outflows, and for mind-produced matter. A state that is an *āsava* is a condition for a state that is an *āsava* by way of object-condition (*ārammaṇapaccaya*): taking the *āsava*s as an object, *āsava*s arise.
A state that is an *āsava* is a condition for a state that is not an *āsava* by way of object-condition: taking the *āsava*s as an object, aggregates that are not *āsava*s arise.

A state that is an *āsava* is a condition for a state that is both an *āsava* and not an *āsava* by way of object-condition: taking the *āsava*s as an object, both *āsava*s and the associated aggregates arise.
A state that is not associated with the taints (anāsava-dhamma) is a condition, by way of object-condition (ārammaṇa-paccaya), for a state not associated with the taints:

giving … [and so on] … virtue … [and so on] … the observance-day ceremony … [and so on] … former [states] … [and so on] … from jhānas … [and so on] … when noble ones, having emerged from the path, review the path, review the fruit, and review Nibbāna;
Nibbāna is a condition for change-of-lineage (gotrabhū) and purification (vodāna).
It is a condition for the path, the fruit, and advertence by way of object-condition.
Noble ones know the taintless defilements that have been abandoned, the taintless defilements that have been suppressed, and the taintless defilements formerly practiced;
they know the eye … [and so on] … the basis, and they perceive the taintless aggregates as impermanent … [and so on] … sorrow arises; with the divine eye, they see forms.
With the divine ear-element, one hears sound; with the knowledge of penetration of minds, one knows the mind of one possessing a mind free from taints;

the base of infinite space [is related] to the base of infinite consciousness …pe… the base of nothingness [is related] to the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception …pe… the visible-form base [is related] to eye-consciousness …pe… the tangible-object base [is related] to body-consciousness …pe… [those] free from taints.

The aggregates are related to the knowledge of the various supernormal powers, the knowledge of penetration into others' minds, the knowledge of recollection of past lives, the knowledge of the passing away and rebirth of beings according to their karma, and the knowledge of the future, as well as to advertence, by way of object-condition.
A state free from taints is related to a state with taints by way of object-condition: having given a gift... [and so forth]... that...

One relishes and delights in it; with that as object, taints arise. [In regard to] virtue … [and so on] … the observance-day ceremony … [and so on] … the past … [and so on] … the jhānas … [and so on] … the eye … [and so on] … one relishes and delights in the bases and the taintless aggregates;
with that as object, taints arise.
A state that is not an *āsava* is a condition, by way of object-condition (*ārammaṇapaccaya*), for a state that is both an *āsava* and not an *āsava*:
having given a gift … [as before] … (second section) one relishes and delights in aggregates that are not *āsavas*;
taking those as an object, *āsavas* and the associated aggregates arise.

States that are both taints and not-taints are a condition, by way of object-condition, for a state that is a taint: taking as object the aggregates associated with taints as well as the taints themselves, taints arise.

States that are both taints and not-taints are a condition, by way of object-condition, for a state that is not a taint: taking as object the aggregates associated with taints as well as the taints themselves, aggregates that are not taints arise.

States that are both taints and non-taints are a condition, by way of object-condition, for states that are both taints and non-taints: taking as object the aggregates that are both taints and associated with taints, there arise taints and the aggregates associated with them.
Predominance:

A state that is a taint is a condition, by way of predominance-condition, for a state that is a taint. Object-predominance: making taints an object of esteem, taints arise. (The three [types] are similar to the object-condition; they should be treated as objects of esteem.)

A state that is not associated with the taints (*anāsava*) is a condition for a state not associated with the taints by way of predominance condition (*adhipatipaccaya*): namely, object-predominance (*ārammaṇādhipati*) and co-nascent predominance (*sahajātādhipati*).

Object-predominance: [Taking] giving … precept … the observance-day ceremony … [former] meritorious deeds … jhānas … the Noble Ones’ paths … the fruits … or Nibbāna as an object of esteem … [or] Nibbāna [is a condition] for the change-of-lineage (*gotrabhū*), purification (*vodāna*), and the path.
It is a condition for its fruit by way of predominance-condition (*adhipatipaccaya*). Taking the eye … [and so on] … the basis (*vatthu*) as estimable, one relishes and delights in it;
taking that as estimable, lust arises and wrong view arises. Co-nascent predominance (*sahajātādhipati*):
a predominance that is not an outflow (*anāsava*) is a condition by way of predominance-condition for its associated aggregates and for mind-originated matter.

A state free from taints (anāsava-dhamma) is a condition for a state with taints (āsava-dhamma) by way of predominance-condition (adhipati-paccaya): as object-predominance (ārammaṇādhipati) and as conascence-predominance (sahajātādhipati).
As object-predominance: one esteems, relishes, and delights in a gift... [and so on] ...in the aggregates free from taints;
esteeming them, taints arise. As conascence-predominance: a predominance free from taints is a condition for the associated taints.
Conditioned by way of predominance condition (*adhipatipaccaya*).

Dependent upon a state that is both an outflow and subject to outflows, there arises a state that is both an outflow and subject to outflows by way of the root condition: namely, the outflow of sensual desire (*kāmāsava*).

Dependent on the taint of views, there is the taint of ignorance (*diṭṭhāsavaṃ paticca avijjāsavo*); [the wheel is to be joined]. Dependent on the taint of existence, there is the taint of ignorance; [the wheel is to be joined]. Dependent on the taint of views, there is the taint of ignorance.

That is to say: dependent on the *āsava* of sensual desire (*kāmāsava*), there arise the *āsava* of views (*diṭṭhāsava*), the *āsava* of ignorance (*avijjāsava*), the associated aggregates, and mind-produced matter; [dependent on] the *āsava* of existence (*bhavāsava*).
